central_topic: Width, initialization scale, and AdamW weight decay in finite-horizon delayed generalization on modulo-97 addition with a fixed embedding-sum GELU network, under right censoring and incomplete final observations.
core_methods: Fixed-architecture hidden-width comparisons at widths 32, 128, and 256 with paired seeds and data splits
AdamW learning-rate, decoupled-weight-decay, and initialization-multiplier interventions
Fixed-reference, width-matched initial-global-norm, and zero-weight-decay comparison arms
Checkpointed training/generalization threshold events, parameter-norm trajectories, and explicitly right-censored delays
comparators: Weight-norm and loss-landscape explanations of grokking
Lazy-to-rich training dynamics as a theoretical comparator, not an observed transition
Circuit-efficiency explanations of grokking, not measured circuit identification
Mechanistic progress measures in modular-addition Transformers, as a different-architecture comparator only
Grokking/double-descent connections and model-size versus training-duration effects, without claiming observed double descent
benchmarks: Programmatically generated addition modulo 97: ordered integer pairs mapped to (a+b) mod 97
Disjoint search/final pools of 4704/4705 pairs from the 9409-pair input universe, with seeded 60% training splits within each pool
result_driven_themes: Reduced initialization at unchanged learning rate and weight decay is associated with higher search-stage mean terminal accuracy; this does not identify weight-norm mediation

No candidate grokking events were recorded in the 6000-update search evaluations; two available width-128 final records have delayed events at a 24000-update horizon on different seeds and a different pool, so this is not a controlled horizon-only comparison
The three available width-32 final records remain right-censored; final width-256 records and one width-128 record are missing, preventing a complete width-response curve
Final evaluation did not qualify and only five of nine planned width-seed records are present; retained events are descriptive evidence, not a validated general law of model size
Matched nominal AdamW shrinkage does not imply matched effective regularization, optimization trajectories, or post-fit decay exposure

queries.query: "Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets" 2201.02177
queries.rationale: User-authorized origin of small algorithmic grokking tasks; establishes the modular-arithmetic benchmark and the distinction between early training fit and later generalization. The actual records require separating short-horizon non-events from longer-horizon delayed events.

The recorded trainer uses AdamW and explicit zero-decay controls. This anchors the distinction between learning-rate-times-decay shrinkage and actual weight-norm dynamics, including the unsuccessful matched-nominal-shrinkage configuration.

Initialization scale, measured global norms, and a matched-initial-norm arm are directly present. The strongest successful search configuration reduces initialization scale, motivating comparison with norm-based explanations without claiming causal norm mediation or cross-domain transfer.

queries.query: "Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics" 2310.06110
queries.rationale: A user-authorized theoretical comparator for width and initialization effects. Its stated two-layer regression setting differs from the recorded modular-addition classification network; no lazy-to-rich transition or frozen-feature baseline was measured here.

Circuit efficiency is an explicit alternative explanation in the task. Width, regularization, and post-fit delay make it a relevant comparator, but the recorded norm/accuracy curves do not measure circuits or establish an efficiency mechanism.

queries.query: "Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability" 2301.05217
queries.rationale: Provides the user-authorized modular-addition mechanistic comparator. Its Transformer setting must be distinguished from this run's two learned input embeddings summed before GELU and a linear classifier; the run supports no architecture switch or Fourier-circuit discovery.

Directly connects delayed generalization with the capacity/generalization literature a width study must position against. Use as a conceptual comparator, not as evidence that the incomplete three-width observations exhibit double descent.

queries.query: "Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt" 1912.02292
queries.rationale: Distinct from the grokking-specific unification: anchors the established distinction between model-size and training-duration dependence. The differing search/final horizons and missing widest-model outcomes make that distinction important, but do not establish a nonmonotonic size law.
